title: Solve it together: count the low-battery days
idea: GUIDED. Count values under a threshold; includes spotting a wrong approach.
problem: Battery readings over 5 days are 80, 15, 40, 10, 95. Count days the battery was under 20.

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: Readings 80, 15, 40, 10, 95. Count days under 20.

Understand -- what is the OUTPUT?
exercises.explanation: The output is a COUNT of low readings (under 20).

exercises.prompt: By hand: which readings are under 20, and how many?
exercises.explanation: 15 and 10 are under 20 -- two of them. The hand count (2) is our check value.

exercises.prompt: Which comparison tests 'under 20' (less than 20, not equal to it)?
exercises.explanation: 'Under 20' means strictly less than, so <. Using <= would wrongly include a reading of exactly 20.

exercises.prompt: A learner plans: 'start the counter at 1 so I don't miss the first one.' Why is that wrong?
options: A counter must start at 0, or every count is one too high
exercises.explanation: Starting at 1 adds a phantom count before any reading is checked. Counters start at 0.

blocks: For each reading, check if it is under 20
If it is, add 1 to the counter
exercises.explanation: Counter at 0, loop, test < 20, add on a match, show. The correct start is 0.
'Under 20' is strictly less than: reading < 20. Only 15 and 10 pass.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the full solution (one reading per pass in `reading`).
exercises.explanation: Counter at 0 (not 1), loop each reading, add 1 when under 20, print the count.

exercises.prompt: It prints 2, matching your hand answer. So...
exercises.explanation: Output (2) matches the hand count (2). Starting the counter at 0 gave the right number.

exercises.prompt: Re-check: readings 5, 19, 20, 21 with the rule 'under 20'. How many?
exercises.explanation: 5 and 19 are under 20; 20 is NOT (it's not less than 20), and 21 isn't. Count is 2 -- the < vs <= detail matters.

exercises.prompt: If the counter had started at 1, this check would have printed 3 instead of 2.
exercises.explanation: True -- a start of 1 adds one too many every time. That's why the corrected plan starts at 0.
